source_text: Hoc unitatis sacramentum, hoc vinculum concordiae inseparabiliter cohaerentis ostenditur quando in Evangelio tunica Domini Jesu Christi non dividitur omnino nec scinditur, sed sortientibus de veste Christi quis Christum indueret, integra vestis accipitur, et incorrupta atque indivisa tunica possidetur. Loquitur ac dicit Scriptura divina: De tunica autem, quia de superiore parte non consutilis, sed per totum textilis fuerat, dixerunt ad invicem: Non scindamus illam, sed sortiamur de ea cujus sit. Unitatem illa portabat de superiore parte venientem, id est de coelo et a Patre venientem, quae ab accipiente ac possidente scindi omnino non poterat, sed totam simul et solidam firmitatem inseparabiliter obtinebat. Possidere non potest indumentum Christi qui scindit et dividit Ecclesiam Christi. Contra denique cum, Salomone moriente, regnum ejus et populus scinderetur, Achias propheta Jeroboam regi obvius factus in campo, in duodecim scissuras vestimentum suum discidit dicens: Sume tibi decem scissuras, quia haec dicit Dominus: Ecce scindo regnum de manu Salomonis, et dabo tibi decem sceptra, et duo sceptra erunt ei propter servum meum David et propter Hierusalem civitatem quam elegi ut ponam nomen meum illic. Cum duodecim tribus Israel scinderetur, vestimentum suum propheta Achias discidit. At vero, quia Christi populus non potest scindi, tunica ejus per totum textilis et cohaerens divisa a possidentibus non est. Individua, copulata, connexa ostendit populi nostri, qui Christum induimus, concordiam cohaerentem. Sacramento vestis et signo declaravit Ecclesiae unitatem.
pass_a_gloss: This sacrament of unity, this bond of inseparably coherent concord is shown when in the Gospel the tunic of Lord Jesus Christ is not divided at all nor torn, but to those casting lots about the garment of Christ who might put on Christ, the whole garment is received, and the untorn and undivided tunic is possessed. Divine Scripture speaks and says: About the tunic, however, because it was not sewn from the upper part, but was woven throughout, they said to each other: Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots about it whose it may be. That tunic carried unity coming from the upper part, that is from heaven and from the Father, which could not be torn at all by the one receiving and possessing, but it obtained the whole and solid firmness inseparably at the same time. He who tears and divides the Church of Christ cannot possess the garment of Christ. On the contrary, when Solomon was dying, and his kingdom and people were being torn, prophet Ahijah, having come across king Jeroboam in the field, tore his garment into twelve tears, saying: Take for yourself ten tears, because the Lord says: Behold, I tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give to you ten scepters, and two scepters will be his because of my servant David and because of Jerusalem city which I chose that I might put my name there. When the twelve tribes of Israel were being torn, prophet Ahijah tore his garment. But truly, because the people of Christ cannot be torn, his tunic, woven throughout and coherent, was not divided by those possessing it. It shows the coherent concord of our people, who put on Christ, individual, coupled, connected. By the sacrament of the garment and by the sign, it declared the unity of the Church.

pass_b_english: The Gospel shows this sacrament of unity and this bond of inseparable concord when it tells us that the tunic of the Lord Jesus Christ was not divided or torn at all. Instead, when the soldiers cast lots to decide who would receive the garment, the whole piece was taken, and the undivided tunic was kept intact. Scripture explains that the tunic was not sewn from a patch, but woven as a single piece throughout. Therefore, the soldiers said to one another, 'Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it, to see whose it is.' This tunic carried the unity that came from above, that is, from heaven and from the Father. Because this unity came from the Father, it could not be torn apart by the one who received it, but it held the whole and solid strength together inseparably. He who tears and divides the Church of Christ cannot possess the garment of Christ. On the contrary, when Solomon was dying, his kingdom and people were divided. The prophet Ahijah met King Jeroboam in the field and tore his own garment into twelve pieces, saying, 'Take for yourself ten pieces, for the Lord says, "Behold, I will tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon and give you ten scepters. Two scepters will remain for him because of my servant David and because of Jerusalem, the city I chose to place my name there."' When the twelve tribes of Israel were divided, the prophet Ahijah tore his garment. But because the people of Christ cannot be divided, his tunic, woven as a single piece and held together, was not torn by those who possessed it. It shows the coherent concord of our people, who put on Christ, as an individual, coupled, and connected body. By the sacrament of the garment and by the sign, it declared the unity of the Church (1 Kings 11:29-32).

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal translation of all clauses. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning, agency, and theological distinctions of the original. The scripture citation (1 Kings 11:29-32) added in Pass B correctly identifies the biblical allusion in the Latin text regarding Ahijah and Jeroboam.
